title: Microsoft Purview: retention based on last accessed date for SharePoint and OneDrive files
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's rollout notice and keeps the separate archiving preview's limitations distinct from Purview retention. The changed licensing source still publishes no last-accessed-specific requirement; the licensing classification should nevertheless reflect the documented general retention entitlement.

claims.claim: The planned capability applies retention to SharePoint and OneDrive items based on when a user last accessed them.
claims.quote: This creates the ability to apply Retention to each SharePoint or OneDrive item based on when it was last accessed by a user.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The rollout is automatic and Microsoft requires no administrator action before rollout.
claims.quote: This rollout will happen automatically by the specified date with no admin action required before the rollout.

claims.claim: Microsoft asks administrators to review their current configuration.
claims.quote: Review your current configuration to determine the impact for your organization.

claims.claim: The announced retention control is called 'When items were last accessed' and will be usable when configuring labels and policies.
claims.quote: After the rollout, admins can use the retention control When items were last accessed when configuring labels and policies.

claims.claim: Microsoft says it will add documentation to the notice before rollout.
claims.quote: Before rollout, we will update this post with new documentation.

claims.claim: Microsoft says deleting obsolete data with the feature will improve Copilot response quality and relevance.
claims.quote: This feature will help delete obsolete data, which will improve the quality and relevance of Microsoft 365 Copilot responses.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether existing retention configurations change automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview last accessed automatically existing; read MC999442, retention, create-retention-policies, and returned results. Availability and rollout are automatic; no passage says existing retention configurations change.

claims.claim: The default enforcement state of this new retention control is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention last accessed licensing default retention policy label LastAccessed retention rule. Read MC999442 and retention guidance: default availability is stated, but default enforcement or changes to existing policies are not.

claims.claim: Existing documented retention start options include when content was created.
claims.quote: When the content was created. The default start of the retention period.

claims.claim: Starting retention when content was last modified is documented only for files in SharePoint, OneDrive and Microsoft 365 Groups locations.
claims.quote: When the content was last modified. Supported only for files in the SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft 365 Groups locations.

claims.claim: Existing documented retention start options include when content was labeled.
claims.quote: Start the retention period from when the content was labeled for documents in SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts, and for email items.

claims.claim: Existing documented retention start options include when an event occurs.
claims.quote: Start the retention period when an event occurs, such as employees leave the organization, or contracts expire.

claims.claim: Learn's retention guidance does not yet describe the announced Purview last-accessed start option.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention last accessed licensing default retention policy label LastAccessed retention rule; read retention, create-retention-policies, New-RetentionComplianceRule and New-ComplianceTag. Documented start choices omit last access.

claims.claim: The separate SharePoint Advanced Management inactive-files policy archives files rather than deleting them.
claims.quote: Inactive files policies in SharePoint Advanced Management help administrators automatically archive eligible SharePoint files based on when they were last accessed.

claims.claim: For the archive preview, last access date is the recorded date a human last accessed the file.
claims.quote: Last access date (LAD) is the recorded date a human last accessed a file.

claims.claim: AI agent, application, script and system access do not update the archive preview's last access date.
claims.quote: AI agent, application, script, and system access don't update it.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Last access date updates for the archive preview can take up to 30 days.
claims.quote: Last access date updates can take up to 30 days. Recent human access might not yet be reflected in the recorded LAD used by an inactive files policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Human access before July 2025 might not have been captured in the archive preview's recorded access history.
claims.quote: Human access before July 2025 might not have been captured, so a recorded LAD can make a file look inactive longer than it really was.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented Purview's definition of access or whether automated access counts as it does for the archive preview.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention last accessed access latency history existing files retain only disposition simulation. Read retention, create-retention-policies, MC999442 and manage-inactive-files; the latter expressly excludes Purview configuration.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published Purview last-accessed retention's access-update latency.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention last accessed access latency history existing files retain only disposition simulation. Read retention and MC999442; the 30-day statement occurs in the separate manage-inactive-files archive guidance.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published Purview last-accessed retention's access-history limits.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention last accessed access latency history existing files retain only disposition simulation. Read retention and MC999442; the July 2025 boundary is documented in separate archive guidance, not for Purview.

claims.claim: No new identity or permission surface is described for this option.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention last accessed licensing default retention policy label LastAccessed retention rule. Read MC999442, retention and get-started-with-data-lifecycle-management permissions; no new feature-specific identity or permission surface is described.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends the Compliance Administrator role group for managing retention policies and labels.
claims.quote: To grant permissions for this limited administration, we recommend that you add users to the Compliance Administrator admin role group.

claims.claim: The announced delete policies make permanent deletion the eventual action, rather than archiving.
claims.quote: Content is permanently deleted at the end of the shortest retention period for the item.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published whether retain-only configurations support the last-accessed trigger.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention last accessed access latency history existing files retain only disposition simulation. Read retention, create-retention-policies and MC999442; the notice specifies delete policies and Learn does not document the trigger.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published whether retain-then-delete configurations support the last-accessed trigger.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention last accessed access latency history existing files retain only disposition simulation. Read retention, create-retention-policies and MC999442; generic retain-and-delete support does not document this unpublished trigger.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an evaluation mode for Purview last-accessed deletion.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention last accessed access latency history existing files retain only disposition simulation. Read retention, New-RetentionCompliancePolicy and manage-inactive-files; available simulation text does not establish this option's evaluation mode.

claims.claim: Disposition review is supported by retention labels, not retention policies.
claims.quote: | Disposition review | No | Yes |

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specifically confirmed disposition review with last-accessed deletion.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention last accessed access latency history existing files retain only disposition simulation. Read retention, MC999442 and disposition search excerpts; none describes disposition review with the announced last-accessed trigger.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how this last-accessed clock applies to files that already exist when a policy is created.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview retention last accessed access latency history existing files retain only disposition simulation; Purview last accessed automatically existing. Read retention, create-retention-policies and MC999442; no feature-specific initialization rule found.

claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because feature-specific licensing is unpublished despite documented general retention entitlements.
claims.quote: For organization-wide, location-wide, or include/exclude retention policies, the following licenses provide user rights: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3, Business Premium
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace licensing.notes with: 'General retention policies are included with Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3 and Business Premium, among other listed plans in the Microsoft Purview service description. Requirements specific to the last-accessed option are not yet published.' This is the standard's product-level licensing understatement, not confirmation of a feature-specific entitlement.

claims.where: summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licensing requirement specific to last-accessed retention.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview last accessed license retention; Purview retention last accessed licensing default retention policy label LastAccessed retention rule. Read the changed Purview service description's retention policy, label and deployment licensing sections; no last-accessed entry found.

claims.claim: No meter is documented specifically for last-accessed retention.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview last accessed billing meter. Read purview-billing-models and the Purview service description; the DLM meter covers AI interactions, not last-accessed SharePoint or OneDrive retention. No feature-specific meter found.

claims.claim: General organization-wide, location-wide and include/exclude retention policy rights include Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3 and Business Premium.
claims.quote: For organization-wide, location-wide, or include/exclude retention policies, the following licenses provide user rights: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3, Business Premium

claims.claim: SharePoint Plan 2 also provides retention policy rights for SharePoint or OneDrive for Business locations.
claims.quote: If the retention policy location is SharePoint or OneDrive for Business, the following licenses also provide user rights: SharePoint Plan 2

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 is among the qualifying licenses required for adaptive retention policy scopes.
claims.quote: If the retention policy uses an adaptive policy scope, then one of the following licenses is required to provide user rights: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW is also listed as a qualifying license for adaptive retention policy scopes.
claims.quote: If the retention policy uses an adaptive policy scope, then one of the following licenses is required to provide user rights: ... Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Archive is the separate archive storage option.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Archive provides the archive storage tier and file reactivation experience.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Archive's storage meter is per GB per month.
claims.quote: Storage consumption is charged at a per-GB monthly rate.

claims.claim: The SharePoint Archive storage meter is charged only when combined archived and active storage exceeds the tenant's included or licensed SharePoint capacity.
claims.quote: This meter is charged only when archived storage plus active storage in SharePoint exceeds the included or licensed allocated SharePoint storage capacity limit of the tenant.

claims.claim: An administrator restricted by assigned administrative units cannot configure a retention policy including SharePoint sites; an unrestricted administrator is required.
claims.quote: If your organization is using administrative units and you're a restricted administrator assigned one or more adminsitrative units, you won't be able to configure a retention policy that includes SharePoint sites or Exchange public folders.

claims.claim: Retention policy creation is reached in the Microsoft Purview portal through Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies. ... Select New retention policy to start the Create retention policy configuration

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy-name> -SharePointLocation <site-url> -OneDriveLocation <onedrive-url> creates the scoped policy object.
claims.quote: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name "Regulation 123 Compliance" ... -SharePointLocation "https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/teams/finance" ... The OneDriveLocation parameter specifies the OneDrive sites to include. You identify the site by its URL value

claims.claim: Creating a functioning retention policy also requires New-RetentionComplianceRule.
claims.quote: Creating a new policy also requires use of the New-RetentionComplianceRule cmdlet. ... Policies are not valid until a rule is added (for retention policies)

claims.claim: New-SPOFileArchivePolicy -Name <n> -PolicyType <t> -LastAccessDateCriteria <months> -IsWhatIfMode $true creates a last-access-date archive policy in simulation mode.
claims.quote: New-SPOFileArchivePolicy [-Name <String>] -PolicyType <SPOFileArchivePolicyType> [-LastAccessDateCriteria <Int32>] ... [-IsWhatIfMode <Boolean>] ... When set to $true, the policy will evaluate which files meet the archiving criteria and report the results

claims.claim: There is no documented admin UI for managing the inactive-files archive policy in the current preview.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint Advanced Management inactive files policy admin UI PowerShell only preview. Opened manage-inactive-files; it states the current preview is available only through PowerShell and Admin Agent support is planned.

claims.claim: The SharePoint inactive-files archive policy is in preview.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is part of the file archive policies feature which is currently in preview.

claims.claim: The archive preview requires a SharePoint Advanced Management entitlement.
claims.quote: Before deploying a policy, confirm: ... Your tenant has the required SharePoint Advanced Management entitlement.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet document the Purview last-accessed wizard option or a cmdlet parameter for it.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview When items were last accessed PowerShell; Purview retention last accessed licensing default retention policy label LastAccessed retention rule. Opened retention, create-retention-policies, New-RetentionComplianceRule and New-ComplianceTag; no last-access option found.

claims.claim: A newly created file archive policy is Inactive.
claims.quote: The policy is created in an Inactive state and must be activated using Set-SPOFileArchivePolicy with -State Active before it takes effect.

claims.claim: Set-SPOFileArchivePolicy -PolicyId <guid> -State Active activates an archive policy.
claims.quote: Set-SPOFileArchivePolicy -PolicyId "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890" -State "Active" ... Activates the specified file archive policy.

claims.claim: A SelectedSites archive policy needs at least one included site before activation.
claims.quote: To activate a SelectedSites policy, at least one site must have been added as an inclusion using Add-SPOSiteToFileArchivePolicy without -Exclude. Excluded sites don't satisfy this requirement.

claims.claim: An Active archive policy with IsWhatIfMode true evaluates and reports without archiving.
claims.quote: | Active | $true | Evaluate and report without archiving files. |

claims.claim: Choosing an archive inactivity period entirely after July 2025 provides more complete observation but does not exclude files with older recorded dates.
claims.quote: For critical content, choose an inactivity period that falls entirely after July 2025. This provides a more complete observation period; it doesn't exclude files with older LADs.

claims.claim: The notice names OneDrive and SharePoint, without stating coverage for Teams, Exchange or Microsoft 365 Groups mailboxes.
claims.quote: Enable admins to apply retention policy or retention label in OneDrive and SharePoint for files that have not been accessed by anyone in the organization after a period of time.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Low reflects the currently evidenced indirect administration cost, not a confirmed absence of future feature-specific licensing or charges.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview last accessed license retention; Purview last accessed billing meter. Read the Purview service description and purview-billing-models; no feature-specific license or meter was found. The page expressly leaves licensing unpublished.
